name: Delhi–Mumbai Expressway
lanes: 8 lanes, access-controlled (built so it can grow to 12)

timeline.event: First 246 km stretch from Sohna to Dausa–Lalsot opens in February
More long stretches open in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat
Around 930 km is open; the Delhi–Vadodara side nears completion while a few Gujarat–Maharashtra packages continue

history: The Delhi–Mumbai Expressway is India's biggest expressway project, linking the national capital with the country's financial capital. Its mainline officially begins at Sohna near the KMP ring road, with an under-construction connector spur linking it back to Delhi's DND Flyway via Faridabad. Instead of following the old highway, it takes a shorter new route through Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, ending near Mumbai's Jawaharlal Nehru Port. The first stretch, from Sohna to Dausa, opened in February 2023, and by mid-2026 roughly 930 km of the corridor is open to traffic while the remaining sections are still being built.
facts: Will be India's longest expressway at about 1,386 km when complete.
Expected to cut the Delhi–Mumbai drive to around 12 hours.
8 lanes wide, designed so it can be expanded to 12 lanes later.
Crosses six states and union territories: Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra.
Has dedicated animal overpasses near the Ranthambore and Mukundra tiger reserves — a first for an Indian expressway.
